newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - COFFEE DUE UP, BUT MOVE SEEN LIMITED.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - COFFEE DUE UP, BUT MOVE SEEN LIMITED.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA40
Coffee is due higher, but technical analysts did not see the impetus needed for a big move either way.
Traders said it was due $40 up on numbers, "but we're looking for around ten," one said.
"Basically, it's pretty neutral," independent technical analyst Elli Gifford said.
There was resistance at $1,650 and then at $1,680, while support was at $1,600, she said.
There could be more activity in store. "We are rapidly moving to the view that coffee, particularly arabica, could soar over the next few weeks," broker GNI said.

New York coffee futures ended sharply higher on Thursday, as speculators resumed buying after Wednesday's modest setback as concerns about near-term supply tightness continued to fuel bullish sentiment, traders said.
Global coffee consumption in 1997/98 is forecast at 101 million bags, rounded, compared with 99.6 million in 1996/97, German trader Bernhard Rothfos GmbH said in its quarterly digest.

Global coffee stocks in the 1997/98 (Oct/Sept) season are forecast to fall to over 31 million bags from opening stocks of 32.36 million on Oct 1, 1997, Rothfos said. It put Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop at 25 million bags compared with a new estimate for 1996/97 of 29 million.

Cool, high pressure currently in Argentina now appears large enough to produce a "glancing blow of cooler weather" to Brazil's coffee belt, however no damaging cold is expected, Weather Services Corp said in an update on Thursday.
